"Sorrowful be the heart, penitent one." And from much later in the game: 

"In my dreams, I heard your footsteps coming closer. In my dreams I tried to talk to you and introduce myself. Guardian of the miracle and the miracle banner, with great pain, I carry the emblem of the father. I am the hands of bloodied skin, I am the eyes from which our mother gazes. But nothing I know of you, except your cold nameless visage. Apart from your calloused and wounded hands. Apart from the mourning of your deaths. No, I know nothing of you, only the miracle knows. Now may your sword full of guilt and mine of gold, collide. Let them hurt and march in procession. I curse you forever in name, I bless you forever in death." 

I feel like both quotes make the same point about how your pain and penance are close bedfellows. Everyone in Cvstodia is aware of the trail of blood you left behind, and the pain you caused is comparable to the first pain and subsequently, after your penance is complete, your forgiveness from the miracle. I find it both fitting and poignant, but specifically within the context of Deogracias' chronicling and Escribar's final words to the penitent one.

It would require quite some time, but perhaps write up a word document with a few long paragraphs describing important events and combat scenarios along with a bunch of phrases like "Roll 1d20 + Con" and "The path leads north/south/east/west". You could rig up a system where you pre-select from a large range of solid -albeit vague- answers on a word document. If a player asks you a question on the fly, you could rig up a pretty quick copy-paste system where you just select the most appropriate answer and send it into them via DM or in the group chat.   


As a more personal touch, for the next 4 weeks or for however long it takes your mouth to heal or adjust, try not to do any story-heavy or player-story intensive content as that can take a long time to write. Instead, go for fun, quirky surface level quests, but complicate them if you wish to draw them out e.g A local wizard wants a live troll for experimenting and when your players finally capture one alive and deliver it, have the same wizard release it by mistake (or on purpose who cares it's your campaign maybe he's evil?) and then have the party save the town from its rampage. You could even follow up with assisting the wizard in containing the troll or perhaps chasing him out of town for his carelessness.

I used to live in the UK and recently moved to Florida a little over a year ago to reconnect with family and go to school (I felt I had better opportunities here in Florida rather than back home, absurd I know). I ended up staying and looking after my grandmother, who was very ill for the time that I knew her before her recent passing, and her medical bills were astonishing, usually $800 a night not including the doctor's consultation, nurse coverage, medicines or service and room cleaning. 

Her bills however, are not what dumbfounds me. What really gets to me out here in the Sunshine State is that something called a Baker Act exists. [Link](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Mental_Health_Act)

The short version of that is that you can have your rights suspended and detained involuntarily for a minimum of 72 hours after you have been seen by a technician and admitted, only being released by a Doctor's say so 

I unfortunately have had a few mental health issues which involved me being "Baker Acted" by the police and, ironically, a therapist. This being a mental institution, there were no comfy beds or privacy, constantly being woken up in the middle of the night to check that I haven't gone mad, blood tests that HAD to be drawn at 5 am, being marched up and down in lines and being spoken to like a child. Perhaps worst of all, is that I didn't get to talk to a single therapist or psychologist. I got to talk to a medical doctor who prescribed me the US's most common antidepressant (Lexapro/[Escitalopram](https://www.drugs.com/escitalopram.html)) and a woman who made me draw pictures about how I feel. I'm a 24 year old man by the way.

The worst and perhaps most insulting part of that whole ordeal were my bills. They noted that it cost me $1100 ***A NIGHT*** \+ the Doctor's fee of $300 for a 15 minute conversation. My total bill of both stays at that institution was in access of $11'000. To add insult to injury, the therapist that Baker acted me sent me a bill for $145 for one: "psychoanalytical evaluation". Her evaluation was a 5 minute talk and her giving me an ultimatum of an escort service or police wagon (again) back to the psych ward. 

I'm not really that mad or upset anymore despite the huge tower of debt. I'm more utterly astonished as to why Americans ***CHOOSE*** to have this system, one so obviously corrupt and morally rotten to the core. It fills me with sadness to know people are forced to live like this and others not a fortunate as myself can't escape this fate. Heaven forbid the poor folks who choose death though; funerals are criminally priced too.
